content.title: About
content.content: Asian mushrooms are dried edible fungi from the Pleurotaceae family, widely used in Asian cuisine. After rehydrating in water they regain their texture and can be cooked like fresh mushrooms, offering a delicate umami aroma and a mildly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried Asian mushrooms are a staple in soups, stews, and stir‑fries.
When properly soaked they expand 5–7 times their original volume.
They are rich in beta‑glucans, which support immune function.
Traditionally used in Chinese medicine to aid digestion.
They store well for long periods without losing flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Mushrooms provide plant‑based protein that helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: They are suitable for weight‑controlled diets due to their modest calorie content.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B2, B3 and B5 vitamins support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Potassium, selenium and copper contribute to heart and nervous system health.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans stimulate activity of immune cells.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms.

items.title: Mycotoxin contamination
items.content: Improperly dried mushrooms can contain toxins; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions may cause gas and bloating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak dried mushrooms in warm water for 20–30 minutes, drain, and use in soups, sauces, stir‑fries or stews. Add them to rice, noodles, or vegetable mixes. For extra aroma, briefly sauté after rehydration.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dried mushrooms in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored they retain quality for 2–3 years. Once rehydrated, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator.
